exercises.title: U3 听力·对话 The Origins of American Food
exercises.speaker: uk_female

transcript.speaker: Host
transcript.text: Welcome back. Today we ask: does America have any food of its own?

transcript.speaker: Guest
transcript.text: Well, most American food actually comes from other cultures and is then mixed into something new.

transcript.speaker: Host
transcript.text: Can you give us an example?

transcript.speaker: Guest
transcript.text: Take nachos. They are just corn chips covered in cheese, first made by a cook for some hungry visitors.

transcript.speaker: Host
transcript.text: And what about gumbo?

transcript.speaker: Guest
transcript.text: Gumbo is a spicy stew invented in New Orleans. It mixes several cooking styles in one pot.

transcript.speaker: Host
transcript.text: So American food is really a mix of the whole world.

transcript.speaker: Guest
transcript.text: Exactly. That spirit of mixing is what makes it special.

exercises.translation_cn: 主持人问美国是否有自己的食物;嘉宾说大多源自别的文化,再融合出新东西;以墨西哥玉米片为例,是裹奶酪的玉米片,由厨师为饥饿的客人首创;秋葵汤是新奥尔良发明的辣味炖菜,一锅融合多种烹饪;主持人总结美式食物是全世界的融合,嘉宾说正是这种融合精神让它特别。

questions.stem: What does the guest say about most American food?
options: It comes from other cultures and is mixed into something new.
It was all invented in America alone.

questions.stem: What are nachos, according to the guest?
Where was gumbo invented?
How is gumbo described?
options: A spicy stew that mixes several styles.

questions.stem: What makes American food special, the guest says?

exercises.title: U3 听力·短文 The First People of California
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: No one knows exactly when the first people arrived in what we now call California.
It is likely that they moved there many thousands of years ago.
After the arrival of the Europeans, the native people suffered greatly.
Many died from new diseases, while others were forced to leave their land.
Even so, some survived, and their culture is still part of the state today.
exercises.translation_cn: 没人确切知道最早的人何时到达今天的加利福尼亚;很可能是数千年前迁来的;欧洲人到来后,原住民遭受了巨大苦难;许多人死于新的疾病,另一些被迫离开家园;尽管如此,仍有人幸存下来,他们的文化至今仍是这个州的一部分。

questions.stem: What is unknown about the first people of California?
options: The exact time when they arrived.

questions.stem: When did they probably move there?
What happened after the Europeans arrived?
Why did many native people die?
options: Because of the cold weather only.

questions.stem: What does the passage say about their culture today?
options: It is still part of the state.

exercises.title: U3 听力·对话 Planning a Visit to Chinatown
exercises.speaker: uk_female

transcript.speaker: Mia
transcript.text: Are you free this afternoon? I'd love to show you Chinatown.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: I'd love to. I've never been there before.

transcript.speaker: Mia
transcript.text: Great. We can enter through the old Dragon Gate first.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Was it really built with materials from China?

transcript.speaker: Mia
transcript.text: Yes, the materials were donated from China many years ago.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Amazing. Can we taste some traditional food too?

transcript.speaker: Mia
transcript.text: Of course. There's food to suit every taste, and the tea shops are wonderful.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Then let's go. I can't wait!

exercises.translation_cn: 米娅问汤姆下午是否有空,想带他逛唐人街;汤姆乐意,说从没去过;米娅说先从龙门进去;汤姆问龙门是否真是用中国的材料建的;米娅说材料多年前由中国捐赠;汤姆想尝尝传统食物;米娅说有适合各种口味的食物,茶馆也很棒;汤姆迫不及待要去。

questions.stem: What does Mia offer to do?
Has Tom been to Chinatown before?
How was the Dragon Gate built?
What does Mia say about the food there?
options: There is food to suit every taste.

questions.stem: How does Tom feel at the end?
options: He is too tired to go.
He no longer wants to go.

exercises.title: U3 听力·短文 An Ancient Instrument
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: In many ethnic minority villages, people still play an old instrument called the lusheng.
This instrument has a history of more than a thousand years.
It is even mentioned in the oldest collection of Chinese poetry.
At festivals, villagers play it while others dance in their best clothing.
Listening to it, visitors feel they have stepped into a different and beautiful world.
exercises.translation_cn: 在许多少数民族村寨,人们仍演奏一种叫芦笙的古老乐器;它有一千多年的历史;甚至在最古老的中国诗歌总集中也被提到;节日里,村民演奏它,其他人则穿着最好的服装起舞;听着它,游客觉得仿佛走进了一个不同而美丽的世界。

questions.stem: Where do people still play the lusheng?
How old is this instrument?
Where is the instrument mentioned?
options: In the oldest collection of Chinese poetry.

questions.stem: What do villagers do at festivals?
options: Play it while others dance in fine clothing.

questions.stem: How do visitors feel when they listen?
options: As if they had entered a different, beautiful world.

exercises.title: U3 听力·对话 Different Tastes in Food
exercises.speaker: uk_female

transcript.speaker: Ann
transcript.text: There's a potluck dinner this weekend. What dish will you bring?

transcript.speaker: Ben
transcript.text: I'm thinking of a spicy stew from my hometown.

transcript.speaker: Ann
transcript.text: Spicy? I'm not sure I can eat very hot food.

transcript.speaker: Ben
transcript.text: Don't worry, I'll make a mild one for you.

transcript.speaker: Ann
transcript.text: Thank you. I'll bring some dumplings, then.

transcript.speaker: Ben
transcript.text: Perfect. So the table will have food from two cultures.

transcript.speaker: Ann
transcript.text: Exactly. That's the best part of sharing a meal.

transcript.speaker: Ben
transcript.text: I agree. See you on Saturday!

exercises.translation_cn: 安说周末有聚餐,问本带什么菜;本想带家乡的辣味炖菜;安说自己吃不了太辣;本说会给她做一份温和不辣的;安道谢,说那她带饺子;本说桌上就有来自两种文化的食物了;安说这正是分享一餐最棒的地方;两人约好周六见。

questions.stem: What event are Ann and Ben talking about?
What dish does Ben plan to bring?
options: A spicy stew from his hometown.

questions.stem: Why is Ann unsure about the dish?
options: She may not be able to eat very hot food.
It takes too long to cook.

questions.stem: What does Ben say he will do for Ann?
options: Make a mild one for her.

questions.stem: What does Ann like best about sharing a meal?
options: Having food from two cultures on the table.

exercises.title: U3 听力·短文 A City of Many Languages
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Some neighbourhoods are so diverse that almost half of the people were born in another country.
Walk down one street and you may hear many different languages being spoken.
People of different backgrounds live side by side, sharing the same shops and streets.
Some worry that life there is hard, but many residents feel quite at home.
For them, the rich mix of cultures is a gift to be treasured, not a problem.
exercises.translation_cn: 有些社区非常多元,近一半的人出生在别的国家;走在一条街上,你可能听到许多种不同的语言;不同背景的人比邻而居,共享同样的商店和街道;有人担心那里生活艰难,但许多居民觉得很自在;对他们来说,丰富的文化融合是一份值得珍惜的礼物,而非难题。

questions.stem: How diverse are these neighbourhoods?
options: Everyone was born in the same town.
Almost half the people were born in another country.

questions.stem: What might you hear walking down one street?

options: Side by side, sharing the same streets.

questions.stem: How do many residents feel about living there?
How do they see the mix of cultures?
